title: GDScript resource retained at shutdown; real-project bisect points to self-referential typed exported Array
body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.6.3-stable official (`4.6.3.stable.official.7d41c59c4`).

### System information

macOS 27.0, arm64, headless import/test execution.

### Issue description

A production project consistently retains one GDScript resource at engine shutdown:

```
ERROR: 1 resources still in use at exit.
Resource still in use: res://src/crowd/nav_node.gd (GDScript)
Leaked instance: GDScriptNativeClass - Reference count: 1
Leaked instance: GDScript - Reference count: 1
```

The affected script declares `class_name NavNode` and exports a typed array of that same class:

```gdscript
@export var manual_connections: Array[NavNode] = []
```

Bisecting the real script isolates the behavior to that declaration:

| Declaration | Shutdown result |
|---|---|
| `Array[NavNode]` | one retained `nav_node.gd` resource |
| `Array[Node]` | no retained resource and no shutdown error |
| restore `Array[NavNode]` | the identical retained resource returns |

The result is stable in both directions. Serialization is unchanged in this project: the scene stores the exported node references as `NodePath` values under either declaration.

This is not test-runner teardown. The identical resource is retained by a bare headless import with no tests and no networking. A full suite adds zero orphan nodes and no additional shutdown leak over the bare-import result.

Important scope note: the self-referential declaration alone is **not yet a complete minimal reproduction**. Four attempted reductions did not reproduce the leak:

1. a standalone `class_name` script exporting `Array[SelfClass]`;
2. the same script instantiated in a scene;
3. an `@tool` variant that creates a debug mesh in `_ready()`;
4. removal/checking of suspected preload cycles (none found).

So the evidence establishes that the declaration is necessary in the real project and that widening it removes the retention, but some additional project condition is also necessary. I am filing the bisect result rather than presenting a synthetic case that does not reproduce.

This appears distinct from #121663: that report requires selecting an editor node with deeply nested `Array[Resource]` properties and leaks inspector UI/RIDs. This case occurs during a bare headless import, requires no inspector selection, and retains exactly the defining GDScript resource.

### Steps to reproduce

In the affected project:

1. Run:
   ```sh
   godot --headless --path . --import
   ```
2. Observe one retained resource at shutdown naming the script above.
3. Change only:
   ```gdscript
   @export var manual_connections: Array[NavNode] = []
   ```
   to:
   ```gdscript
   @export var manual_connections: Array[Node] = []
   ```
4. Run the same command; shutdown is clean.
5. Restore `Array[NavNode]`; the identical retained-resource report returns.

### Minimal reproduction project

Not yet available. The real-project line-level bisect is deterministic, but the four reductions listed above do not carry the additional condition needed to reproduce. I can continue reducing from the real project if maintainers can suggest likely metadata/class-registration conditions worth preserving.
